answer: Epoch Signature Drift Rule. Each identity signs a random challenge every epoch, and its signing rhythm and error profile must stay within a bounded distance of its own prior history. An attacker spawning many identities must build and sustain plausible long histories for each one, not just pass a single gate. Every clone is a hollow shell that fails drift checks within two epochs. Maintaining cover costs continuous per-identity compute and monitoring; a grove of fakes becomes a liability, while honest agents pass trivially. Old histories cannot be copied across a meadow of new keys.
